assessment.nobel_worthiness: The BLP framework for estimating demand and market equilibrium with differentiated products, together with Pakes's dynamic industry models, changed how empirical industrial organisation is done. It is also standard in merger analysis, antitrust, trade and health economics. Impact beyond its home subfield is very large, and the work ties data to theory in a way the committee has long valued. Industrial organisation has not been recognised since 2014.
assessment.attribution: Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes are the clearest core, with the 1995 BLP paper as the anchor and Pakes's earlier and later dynamic work reinforcing his claim. Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin also made real contributions, but a three-person prize captures the central idea cleanly.
assessment.maturity: More than three decades of validation and routine use in academia, competition authorities and industry. The timing is fully mature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer to include Bresnahan or Reiss for the earlier empirical-IO tradition.
Whether the Pakes dynamic-model strand and the BLP demand strand are better treated as one discovery or two.
My assessment of the relative contributions rests on general knowledge, not independently checked sources.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Melitz model and the Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple work on exporters versus FDI put firm heterogeneity at the centre of trade theory. They changed both the theory of gains from trade and the empirical agenda. This is foundational, widely taught and heavily used in policy analysis. Trade has not been honoured since Krugman in 2008.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the pivotal paper, and Helpman's broader contributions to trade theory strengthen the case for a joint award. Redding's quantitative and spatial extensions are important but more derivative, so I would leave him out of a minimal award. Bernard, Eaton and Kortum are strongly related and not credited on this ballot entry, which is a possible attribution risk.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of confirmation across theory, structural estimation and policy work. Timing is mature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would rather give a trade prize to Helpman with Grossman (B047) or to the firm-heterogeneity strand.
Credit overlap with Bernard-Eaton-Kortum-Jensen, who are not listed here.
Whether Redding's quantitative trade work should be included.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki-Moore (1997) provides the canonical model of how collateral constraints amplify and propagate shocks across the cycle. It is central to modern macro-finance and has shaped thinking on the financial crisis and on the real effects of credit frictions. As a finance-and-contracting theorist I see a close link to incomplete-contract foundations, since the model relies on limited enforcement and asset-backed lending.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are the clearest pairing, because the credit-cycles mechanism is theirs. Gertler and Gilchrist belong to the related financial-accelerator and empirical strand. Bernanke and Gertler's accelerator work is adjacent to the 2022 prize, so a prize here should rest on the collateral-cycle contribution and not on a repeat of that theme.
assessment.maturity: Nearly thirty years of influence, with extensions in banking, monetary and macroprudential models.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize on banking and financial crises.
Whether the committee would want the financial-accelerator strand (Gertler, Gilchrist) included.
Quantitative empirical validation of the mechanism is more mixed than its theoretical influence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology and the China-shock evidence reshaped understanding of labour demand, wage inequality and the distributional effects of trade and automation. The combination of credible identification, large policy impact and relevance to current debates is strong.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central to both the task approach and the trade-shock work, and Hanson's trade-shock and local labour market evidence is essential. Katz's long-running work on skill-biased change is foundational for the inequality framing. Dorn is a key co-author on the China shock. Acemoglu and Restrepo, who are closely related and already honoured in part, are not on this entry, so the boundaries of the discovery are somewhat blurry.
assessment.maturity: Roughly two decades of evidence and debate. Some findings have been refined or contested, but the core contribution is established.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 prize and the work of Acemoglu and Restrepo.
Whether the task framework and the trade-shock work are one discovery.
Choosing three from four credited names is a judgment about relative contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mian and Sufi showed with granular data that household leverage and credit supply drove the housing boom and the severity of the Great Recession. This changed macro-finance by joining microdata with macroeconomic outcomes. The work is influential in both academic and policy debates, and it uses real contract and household balance-sheet data in the empirical-finance tradition.
assessment.attribution: The pair is tightly linked through a sustained joint research programme and a clear core idea. Campbell is a major household-finance figure but belongs to a different contribution.
assessment.maturity: The main papers are about 10 to 15 years old. Consequential and widely confirmed, though somewhat less time-tested than the older candidates above.
uncertainties: Some debate on the interpretation of the credit-supply versus expectations channels.
The shorter track record than other candidates.
The prior 2022 prize on financial crises overlaps thematically.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The law-and-finance programme established that legal institutions and investor protection systematically relate to financial development, ownership structure and growth. It created a major empirical research field in corporate finance and comparative institutions. Its impact is very large, though the causal interpretation of legal origins has been debated.
assessment.attribution: The 1997-98 papers by La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer and Vishny are the anchor. A three-person limit forces a choice between Vishny and one of the others, and Shleifer's broader contributions in finance and behavioural economics add to his claim. This is a real attribution difficulty.
assessment.maturity: Nearly thirty years of influence. The core findings have been challenged and refined, so confirmation is partial.
uncertainties: Persistent methodological criticism of the legal-origins identification and of data coding.
Exclusion of Vishny from a three-person award.
Overlap with the 2024 institutions prize, which made the committee's institutional-economics interest evident.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities, the Calvo pricing device, the Taylor rule and the Woodford synthesis form the working framework of modern central banking. Policy impact is enormous and sustained. Yet the framework has been tested hard by the financial crisis and the post-pandemic inflation episode.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is diffuse. Calvo, Taylor, Woodford, Galí, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets each built a different piece. Any three-person selection leaves out comparably important contributors. Gertler's accelerator work overlaps with the 2022 prize.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with decades of use. The post-2020 inflation experience gives new evidence, and its implications for the framework are unsettled.
uncertainties: Difficulty of drawing a defensible three-person boundary among eight credited names.
Open questions about how well the framework performed in the post-pandemic inflation period.
Possible preference for a narrower macro prize elsewhere.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The construction of long-run top-income series from tax data transformed measurement of inequality and shaped public debate and research in many countries. The data-building contribution is substantial, and it supports a large empirical literature. The interpretive and theoretical claims about wealth dynamics are more contested than the measurement work.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez are the core of the top-income-share research programme. Zucman's wealth and offshore-wealth work is more recent and has had less time to be evaluated. Atkinson, who is not on this entry, was a key early pioneer, which raises a priority question. Saez is also credited in B035.
assessment.maturity: The top-income series work is two decades old and well established. Later wealth-tax and offshore-wealth findings are less settled.
uncertainties: Methodological debate over distributional national accounts and measured trends in top shares.
Priority issues with Atkinson and Kuznets-tradition work.
Political salience, which may affect committee deliberations independent of scientific merit.
